a new modeling approach to the effect of antimicrobials on heterogeneous microbial populations is proposed.

we develop a mathematical framework that uses the concept of moments of a distribution to describe the effect of antimicrobials on microbial populations and that we present simplifications that lead to easily applicable approximation tools.

the effect of antimicrobials on heterogeneous microbial populations, in particular with the emergence of resistance.
the development and application of mathematical methods for the analysis of experimental data on antimicrobial resistance.
the development of mathematical methods that can be used to analyze the effect of antimicrobials on heterogeneous microbial populations.

the presented approach is a promising new method to model the effect of antimicrobials on heterogeneous microbial populations.

the proposed modeling framework can be a valuable tool in the development of novel antimicrobial agents and strategies to combat antimicrobial resistance.

the use of cumulants is a powerful tool for modeling and analyzing the effect of antimicrobials on heterogeneous populations.
